articles.title: Your API Can Create the Customer—and Still Be Broken
articles.excerpt: A successful POST /customers response does not prove that your API is correct. It only proves that one business operation worked under one specific set of conditions. Modern APIs are not just business…
articles.body: A successful POST /customers response does not prove that your API is correct. It only proves that one business operation worked under one specific set of conditions. Modern APIs are not just business functions. They are also implementations of a communication protocol. Clients depend on more than the response body: HTTP methods status codes request and response headers content types authentication behavior caching directives content negotiation idempotency consistent error handling When these rules are violated, the API may appear healthy during a happy-path test while still breaking clients, integrations, SDKs, proxies, gateways, or production workflows.
articles.author: Liudas

articles.title: Introducing SerpApi's OpenCode Plugin
articles.excerpt: OpenCode is an open-source, model-agnostic AI coding agent that runs locally on your machine. It can edit files, run terminal commands, and work across multiple repos at once. Because it's model-agnos…
articles.body: OpenCode is an open-source, model-agnostic AI coding agent that runs locally on your machine. It can edit files, run terminal commands, and work across multiple repos at once. Because it's model-agnostic, a lot of developers pair it with local LLMs like Ollama or LM Studio, so their code and data never leave their machine. But OpenCode can't search the web for live data unless you give it access. You can do that with the SerpApi OpenCode plugin . It gives OpenCode access to Google, YouTube, Amazon, Walmart, and dozens of other search engines through a single tool call. What is an OpenCode Plugin? Plugins and Skills sound similar, but they do different jobs. Skills automate boring workflows, tasks where you'd otherwise repeat the same instructions every time.

articles.title: What did your last silent failure actually cost you?
articles.excerpt: Workflows that finish green while nothing happened — the threads are full of them. What I can’t find anywhere is the money. When it last happened — what did it cost? Refund, lost client, hours of digg…
articles.body: Workflows that finish green while nothing happened — the threads are full of them. What I can’t find anywhere is the money. When it last happened — what did it cost? Refund, lost client, hours of digging? What kind of workflow was it? Did you build something for it afterwards, or decide it wasn’t worth the time? Have you ever paid for a tool specifically to catch this? If yes, what and how much. If no, what would have had to be true? Asking because one person here told me diagnosing this is billable work for a consultancy, so a tool that shortens diagnosis shortens the invoice. Someone else said it’s unbillable firefighting. Opposite answers, and I can’t tell which is more common.

articles.title: The live realtor model passed. The goodbye failed. published: true
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Kaggle Benchmarking Challenge I run a voice CRM for a realtor. The agent is supposed to take a lead over the phone: hear a fact, save it, ask for the one missing detail, a…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Kaggle Benchmarking Challenge What I Benchmarked I run a voice CRM for a realtor. The agent is supposed to take a lead over the phone: hear a fact, save it, ask for the one missing detail, and stay on the line until the realtor says that is all. In production it kept missing that script. It went silent after saving a field. A phone number made it skip the email and jump toward the close. It asked again for a name or a budget it had just been given. It stored "call him Friday" and never said Friday. It saved and hung up before asking whether that was everything. I turned those five failures into five Kaggle tasks. The tools return only the fields they saved. They do not hand the model its next sentence.

articles.title: The Test Passed Until the Cookie Banner Showed Up
articles.excerpt: Here's a browser automation scenario I've seen some version of many times. You create a test. It runs 100 times. Everything looks great. Then on execution 101: Click "Start Free Trial" FAILED Element…
articles.body: Here's a browser automation scenario I've seen some version of many times. You create a test. It runs 100 times. Everything looks great. Then on execution 101: Click "Start Free Trial" FAILED Element is not clickable You rerun it. Passes. Run it again. Passes. So someone labels it: flaky and moves on. Except maybe it wasn't flaky. Maybe the button wasn't clickable because a consent banner appeared 300 milliseconds before the click. Maybe Google Tag Manager injected something. Maybe a third-party chat widget changed the layout. Maybe a personalization script ran slowly. Maybe the browser was waiting for a WebSocket message. Maybe the application was technically loaded, but not actually ready. Modern browser automation has a funny problem. The testing frameworks have become much better.
articles.author: Markus Gasser

articles.title: How to Build an AI-Powered Log Summarizer for DevOps
articles.excerpt: Debugging a production incident means combing through hundreds of thousands of log lines. By the time you find the root cause, the outage has already cost you an hour. An LLM-backed log summarizer doe…
articles.body: Debugging a production incident means combing through hundreds of thousands of log lines. By the time you find the root cause, the outage has already cost you an hour. An LLM-backed log summarizer doesn't replace your observability stack — but it gives your on-call engineer a head start that matters. The Problem with Raw Logs Log aggregation tools like Loki, Elasticsearch, and Datadog are excellent at storing and searching logs, but they leave interpretation entirely to you. You run a query, you get 10,000 lines, and you start scrolling. The gap isn't storage or retrieval — it's comprehension . You need someone (or something) to read a window of logs and say: "Between 14:23 and 14:31, the payment service returned 503 errors on every POST to /checkout.

articles.title: WILDCASE: The World Is the Case File — An Outdoor Mystery Game That Gets You Off Your Screen
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass WILDCASE is an outdoor mystery-investigation game that turns a walk in the park into a detective case. You recei…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass WILDCASE: The World Is the Case File 🔍🌳 What I Built WILDCASE is an outdoor mystery-investigation game that turns a walk in the park into a detective case. You receive a classified dossier, put your phone in your pocket, and go outside. You hunt for real physical evidence (a metal gate, weathered bark, brick masonry, a circular fastener), take a 2-5 second scan to verify it, eliminate suspects, and finally name the culprit. Most "get outside" apps pull you away from your phone and still end up glued to a screen. WILDCASE inverts that. The phone is an intermittent field instrument; the world is the game board.

articles.body: TL;DR scrcpy v5.0 brings hardware decoding, which essentially shifts video decoding from the CPU to the GPU, reducing desktop CPU usage by up to 10x, saving power, and potentially lowering input latency. The v5.0 release also introduces official native Windows on ARM64 binaries optimized for Snapdragon-powered laptops. Other changes in this release include the ability to capture all audio streams in audio playback capture mode, improved video buffering, and fixes for UHID keypress dropping bugs. articles.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
articles.excerpt: This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current syst…
articles.body: This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things , barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer . Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash . AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen. Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.
